claims.summary: For X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2 and l_1 the Leighton-Shor scale (2^(-l_1) >= (log N)^(3/4)/sqrt N), with probability tending to one, for every j with 1 <= j <= l_1: (a) every closed simple curve C traced on the grid of mesh 2^(-j) has |sum_i (1_{int C}(X_i) - lambda(int C))| <= L sqrt N l(C) ((log_2(2^(j+3) l(C)))^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)); (b) every H constant on the cells has |sum_i H(X_i) - N int H| <= L sqrt N (j^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)) V_j(H), V_j the cell variation (inner jumps times 2^(-j), plus the boundary ring against the best constant). (c) V_j(H) <= 4 times its inner variation (median constant; boundary ring at most three times the inner boundary). For Lipschitz G its cell averages have V_j at most 8 int(|d_1 G| + |d_2 G|).
claims.assessment: Working proof: the chaining of Section 4.7 of Talagrand's monograph restricted to the coarser mesh (count of curves N_(k+j+1), gamma_(1,2) bound of Proposition 4.7.10 by inclusion, valid for every k by Section B.2, Lemma 4.7.9, Theorem 4.5.16, bounded differences with a sqrt(log N) deviation for the union over (j, tau, k), Bernstein for the outside term when k<0), a winding-number split of a union of cells into simple curves, the layer-cake formula, and a column-and-row walk for the boundary ring of a set of area at most 1/2; the corollary by a translation sweep.
claims.rationale: A tool for the coarea mechanism of the third route review: the Leighton-Shor factor is the logarithm of a boundary component's length in mesh units, so coarse or short structures pay less than (log N)^(3/4).
claims.next_action: Relate the component lengths of a class function's level sets to the gradient levels they cross, first at two levels.

relationships: A tool toward the coarea mechanism for this conjecture; it bounds the cell-averaged part of any class function.
At the finest mesh j = l_1, part (a) has the monograph's (log N)^(3/4) order for curves; the lower bound's Leighton-Shor sets live at that mesh.
